selected_backend.semantic_companion: CPython stdlib symtable (available for future symbol IR)
selected_backend.redistribution: bundled CPython runtime through the existing PyInstaller distribution

candidates.ast_fidelity: high semantic AST fidelity for syntax supported by the running interpreter
candidates.symbol_resolution: scope/name binding available through symtable; no full cross-module type/call resolution
candidates.common_ir_conversion: lowest cost; current adapter already emits ModuleIR

candidates.ast_fidelity: full-fidelity concrete syntax tree; preserves formatting
candidates.symbol_resolution: ScopeProvider and QualifiedNameProvider metadata; not full arbitrary attribute/type resolution
candidates.packaging: manageable but adds an external package/native build surface

candidates.symbol_resolution: syntax only; semantic/symbol layer must be built separately
candidates.incomplete_source_recovery: strong relative advantage through error-tolerant incremental parsing
candidates.packaging: manageable native/parser dependency; additional binding required

selection_reasons: Current Common IR is structural and already maps directly from stdlib ast.
No extra runtime or native dependency is required for the Windows onedir distribution.
symtable provides compiler scope data without leaking compiler-specific objects past the adapter boundary.
LibCST adds concrete-syntax fidelity that Tomiya does not currently consume enough to justify a primary-backend swap.
tree-sitter-python is retained as a future fallback candidate for incomplete/editor-buffer source.
known_limits: Syntax coverage follows the Python interpreter version used to run Tomiya.
The selected backend does not perform complete cross-module type, overload, or call-target inference.
Incomplete source raises a normalized unsupported_syntax backend error.
